name: Ronald Ross
summary: British physician and researcher who demonstrated mosquito transmission of malaria and developed mathematical models of disease.

name: George Macdonald
summary: Medical entomologist and epidemiologist who refined the mathematical theory of malaria transmission.

name: Patrick Manson
summary: Physician who first demonstrated mosquitoes transmit a blood-borne pathogen (filarial worm).

name: Hilda Hudson
summary: Mathematician who co-authored papers on a priori pathometry with Ross.

name: Alfred Lotka
summary: Mathematician who analyzed and extended Ross's malaria models.

name: India
summary: Country where Ross conducted research while serving in a military post.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Country where Ross discussed malaria with Manson.

name: Sierra Leone
summary: Country visited by Ross for a malaria expedition.

name: Mauritius
summary: Island nation Ross visited to advise on malaria control.

name: Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine
summary: Institution that conducted the malaria expedition to Sierra Leone.

name: Ross Institute
summary: Research institute where Macdonald served as Director.

name: The Prevention of Malaria
summary: Book by Ross containing his second malaria transmission model.

name: thick film
summary: Microscopy method developed by Ross to increase sensitivity of parasite detection.

name: a priori pathometry
summary: Term coined by Ross to describe the scientific activity of modeling transmission dynamics.
